Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
150 AM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Mild temperatures with dry conditions nearly areawide through
  Sunday morning. 

* Low chances (20% or less) for light rain showers along the OR
  border late tonight. 

* Rain and high elevation snow returns late Sunday into Tuesday, 
  with increasing winds and stronger ridgetop gusts especially 
  Sunday through Sunday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

The mild and cloudy weather pattern continues for much of the
remaining holiday weekend through Sunday morning, with only a
low-end (20% or less) chance of light rain showers near the OR
border tonight as a weak upper disturbance moves across the
Pacific NW. Otherwise, the main effect of this quick-moving 
weather system will be increasing west winds for Sierra ridges  
later today and especially tonight with gusts 55-65 mph. Highs
today through Sunday remain above late November averages, mainly
in the mid 50s-lower 60s, except cooling about 5-10 degrees Sunday
for Sierra locations and northeast CA/far northwest NV as the next
storm approaches. 

This storm will bring gusty winds to higher elevations starting
Saturday night, with the peak winds arriving late Sunday afternoon
through Sunday night and also mixing down to lower elevations.
Expect choppy conditions on Lake Tahoe, southwest gusts of 30-40 
mph (and a 30-60% chance of gusts above 40 mph near the
US-395/I-580 corridor) and Sierra ridge gusts of 80+ mph. While
rising snow levels above 8000-8500 feet will limit snow impacts to
higher peaks around Tahoe (1-4") and maybe Mt. Rose Summit (up to
2"), a short burst of heavier rainfall with even a 15-20% chance
of thunder is targeting the Sunday evening period from western 
Lassen County southward to the Tahoe basin. While winter
conditions are less likely, those wrapping up their Sierra and
northeast CA holiday travel Sunday evening can expect wet and 
windy road conditions with ponding of water--especially where snow 
cover is present. Most of western NV should be largely shadowed 
out of much rainfall, except for a brief round of showers Sunday 
evening along this storm's trailing cold front.

After a short break during the day on Monday, the next storm 
brings increasing rain and mountain snow chances by late Monday 
afternoon or evening, continuing through Monday night with a 
period of rain spreading farther into western NV compared to 
Sunday's storm. Snow levels are still on the higher side, mainly 
7000-7500 ft for the Sierra. The main upper low then follows on 
Tuesday, but confidence on this storm's track is lower, with 
scenarios ranging from a decent hit for the Sierra to a nearly 
complete miss (especially from Tahoe northward) as several 
scenarios drop the low farther south across CA. Recent storms 
(after the Nov. 18-20 storm) have underperformed or even 
completely fallen apart, so keep posted to our forecast updates as
we get closer to December. Beyond Tuesday, the pattern remains 
open to additional storms through the first weekend of December, 
but also potential for a longer break up to 2-3 days between 
storms. MJD

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light winds and widespread high level
  clouds, followed by a thicker mid-high level cloud deck later
  today. Valley inversions may produce minor slantwise visibility
  reductions this morning. Increasing west FL100 winds (gusts to 
  55 kt) bring increased turbulence and periods of LLWS late this 
  evening and overnight. 

Regional Outlook: 

* VFR for all main terminals, except patchy FZFG with LIFR
  conditions for KTRK through 15-16Z this morning. FZFG chances
  decrease to less than 30% Saturday morning as thicker clouds and
  increasing FL100 winds (gusts to 55 kt) move into the area.
  These winds will bring increased turbulence and periods of LLWS
  late this evening and overnight for all main terminals. Valley
  inversions may produce minor slantwise visibility reductions
  this morning for KCXP/KMEV. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with widespread mid-high level cloud cover and
  light surface winds continue through Saturday. West FL100 winds
  decrease from Saturday morning through evening, then increase
  while shifting to SW late Saturday night through Sunday night
  with turbulence and LLWS potential returning. Surface winds 
  also increase at all sites Sunday afternoon-night, with periods 
  of rain (and even a 15% chance for lightning) with MVFR/brief 
  IFR for KTRK-KTVL, while other sites have a lower 30-50% chance 
  of lighter rain showers Sunday evening and overnight. 
  
MJD
